limits.note: chip, not board. Table 625 Digital IO characteristics (p. 616): IIOVDD_MAX maximum total IOVDD current 50 mA (sum of all current sourced by GPIO and QSPI pins) and IIOVSS_MAX 50 mA (sum sunk). The QSPI flash pins share this budget.
chip, not board. Table 622 Absolute maximum ratings for digital IO (p. 614): IOVDD max 3.63 V. Applies when 3V3(OUT) is driven from outside.

Pico datasheet section 2.3 Recommended operating conditions (pp. 10-11): VSYS max 5.5 V. RT6150A/B Recommended Operating Conditions (p. 4): supply input voltage 1.8 to 5.5 V (absolute maximum 6 V on VIN).
Pico datasheet section 2.3 Recommended operating conditions (p. 10): VBUS 5 V +/- 10 %, so 5.5 V.

typical.note: chip, not board. Table 637 Power Consumption (p. 623), BOOTSEL mode - Active, typical average: DVDD 9.4 mA + IOVDD 1.2 mA + USB_VDD 1.4 mA = 12.0 mA. On the Pico, DVDD comes from the on-chip LDO fed from 3.3 V, so its input current is about the DVDD current. In BOOTSEL the bootrom's USB bootloader chains clk_sys from clk_usb (48 MHz; RP2040-E16 erratum, p. 634); user code at the default 125 MHz draws more DVDD (Table 635, p. 622, gives per-MHz figures per peripheral). Excludes flash, LED and board extras (see unaccounted).

peak.note: Worst-case device, BOOTSEL mode - Active, Table 637 (p. 623) maximum average: DVDD 14.7 + IOVDD 4.3 + USB_VDD 2.0 = 21.0 mA, across temperature extremes and maximum voltage; chip, not board.
peak.label: busiest code

minVolts.note: chip, not board. Table 634 Power Supply Specifications (p. 622): IOVDD and VREG_VIN min 1.62 V. USB_VDD needs 3.135 V and ADC performance is compromised below 2.97 V (Table 634 note c), so USB and the ADC fail before this.

ron.note: Pico R3 schematic (RPI-PICO-R3-PUBLIC-SCHEMATIC.pdf in the design files): micro-USB J1 VBUS is wired straight to the VBUS net and pin 40, no part in series. 10 mohm stands for the copper trace (assumed; not measured).

vf.note: D1 on the Pico R3 schematic and BOM is an onsemi MBR120VLSFT1G. Read from Figure 1 Typical Forward Voltage (p. 3), TJ = 25 C curve at IF = 0.1 A (the graph floor): about 0.245 V. The tabulated values are maxima: 0.275 V at 0.1 A, 0.315 V at 0.5 A, 0.340 V at 1.0 A, TJ = 25 C (Electrical Characteristics, p. 2).

vout.note: RT6150B-33GQW (U2 on the Pico R3 schematic and BOM), fixed 3.3 V output option (p. 1 Features: "Fixed 3.3V and Adjustable Output Voltage Options").

efficiency.note: Read from Typical Operating Characteristics (p. 7), PS = L (the Pico default, GPIO23 low): "Efficiency vs. Input Voltage" at VIN about 4.7 V gives about 78 % at 10 mA and about 89 % at 100 mA; "Buck-Boost 3.3V Efficiency" at 10 to 30 mA lies between about 69 % (VIN 5.5 V) and 87 % (VIN 4.2 V). 0.8 for the Pico's 10 to 50 mA at VSYS about 4.7 V.

vinMin.note: RT6150A/B Recommended Operating Conditions (p. 4): supply input voltage 1.8 to 5.5 V; input UVLO falling 1.55 V typ (1.4 V min), rising 1.65 V typ (1.8 V max), Electrical Characteristics (p. 4). Pico datasheet section 2.3 (pp. 10-11): VSYS min 1.8 V. Below vout the converter boosts (see notes).

vinMax.note: RT6150A/B Recommended Operating Conditions (p. 4): supply input voltage max 5.5 V (absolute maximum 6 V).

ioutMax.note: p. 1 Features: "Up to 800mA Continuous Output Current". The "Maximum Output Current vs. Input Voltage" curve (p. 7) shows the limit falls to about 350 mA at VIN = 1.8 V. The Pico datasheet pin descriptions (p. 8) recommend keeping the 3V3 pin load below 300 mA.

iq.note: Electrical Characteristics (p. 4): quiescent current 60 uA typ at IOUT = 0 mA, PS = 0 V (Power Save Mode), VIN = VOUT = 3.6 V.

outputResistance.note: Default drive strength 4 mA (PADS_BANK0 GPIO DRIVE reset 0x1 = 4MA, Table 341, p. 301). Read from Figure 171 typical IV curves (p. 618), 4 mA setting at 10 mA: output high about 2.85 V, (3.3 - 2.85) / 0.01 = 45 ohm; output low about 0.30 V, 0.30 / 0.01 = 30 ohm; mean about 38 ohm. Worst case from Table 625 (p. 616): VOH min 2.62 V and VOL max 0.5 V at the selected current. Chip, not board.

pullup.note: Table 625 (p. 616): RPU pull-up resistance min 50 kohm, max 80 kohm, no typical; midpoint taken. Chip, not board.

pulldown.note: Table 625 (p. 616): RPD pull-down resistance min 50 kohm, max 80 kohm, no typical; midpoint taken. Chip, not board.

inputLeakage.note: chip, not board. Table 625 (p. 615): pin input leakage current IIN max 1 uA.

notes: Board: Pico R3 design files https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/pico/RPi-Pico-R3-PUBLIC-20200119.zip (schematic and BOM) and the Pico datasheet section 4.4 Powerchain (p. 20): micro-USB VBUS -> D1 MBR120VLSFT1G -> VSYS -> U2 RT6150B-33GQW buck-boost (L1 2.2 uH) -> 3V3; 3V3_EN is the RT6150 EN pin, pulled up to VSYS by 100 kohm.

The RT6150 is a buck-boost, modelled as a "buck" rail with vinMin (1.8 V) below vout (3.3 V): it boosts when VSYS is below 3.3 V and bucks above (Pico datasheet section 4.4, p. 20: "can seamlessly switch from buck to boost mode ... ~1.8 V to 5.5 V"). The solver's buck model holds vout across the whole vinMin..vinMax window, which is that behaviour.
Buck-boost reverse is "blocks" and offPath "open": RT6150A/B p. 1 "VOUT Disconnected from VIN during Shutdown"; reverse conduction while running is not documented.
3V3_EN is not modelled: shorting it to ground disables the converter (Pico datasheet pin descriptions, p. 8), which this format cannot express.
USB-to-VBUS rail reverse is "body-diode", but a "ron" switch conducts both ways in this solver anyway, matching the real direct connection (VBUS pin and the USB connector are one net).
VBUS diode reverse is "blocks": D1 is a Schottky from VBUS to VSYS (reverse current max 0.60 mA at rated 20 V, 25 C, MBR120VLSF p. 2).
VSYS domain nominal 4.7 V: 5 V USB minus the D1 drop.

GPIO pins: GP0-GP22 and GP26-GP28 (ADC0-ADC2). GPIO23 (SMPS PS), GPIO24 (VBUS sense), GPIO25 (LED) and GPIO29 (VSYS/3 sense) are on-board only. Left out: RUN, 3V3_EN, ADC_VREF, SWCLK, SWDIO, power, ground, USB.

No per-pin current limit: the RP2040 datasheet gives no per-pin current rating, only VOH/VOL at the 2/4/8/12 mA drive settings, which it says "are not hard limits" (section 5.5.3.5, p. 617). The package total (50 mA) is the only current limit.
unaccounted: The board's W25Q16JV flash chip on 3V3: no number from the schematic or a measurement (it shares the RP2040 IOVDD budget for its pin currents).

The board's green LED on GPIO25, through a 470 ohm resistor (paired from the parts list, not traced on the schematic): drawn only when firmware lights it; about (3.3 V - 2 V) / 470 ohm = 2.8 mA (LED Vf assumed).
The board's USB voltage sense divider (5.6 kohm + 10 kohm) to GND: about 5 V / 15.6 kohm = 0.32 mA on VBUS (arithmetic from the schematic).
The board's VSYS sense divider (200 kohm + 100 kohm): about 4.7 V / 300 kohm = 16 uA; 3V3_EN 100 kohm pull-up to VSYS (no current unless 3V3_EN is pulled low, then VSYS / 100 kohm).
Crystal oscillator and the RP2040 at clocks other than BOOTSEL's 48 MHz: the draw uses the BOOTSEL figures.
